page: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores using the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) powered by AWS Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz. The system provides 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 96 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core capabilities. The multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmark scores 380,393.63, placing it in the top 10% of tested servers, while single-core performance remains in the average tier at 2,006.19. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 27,753.18 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 340.16 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 scales to 1,910.26 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance achieves 511.16 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and scores 61,797.63 on PassMark database operations.

Tradeoffs are evident in LLM inference and single-threaded tasks. While prompt processing for a 7B model reaches a top-tier 383.91 tokens per second, text generation speeds drop to an average 10.1 tokens per second, and text generation for a small 135M model is poor at 12.87 tokens per second. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. This instance is suited for highly parallelized, compute-bound workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, high-throughput database operations, and CPU-based container orchestration.
